description: The plot titled “Sparsity Ratio of SDPA Output, Threshold 1e-3” illustrates how the sparsity ratio of SDPA output varies across model layers for three conditions. The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately layers 0 through 23 with major tick labels shown at 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. The y-axis is labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 up to about 0.9 with labeled ticks at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8. Three lines are shown: a blue dashed line (no markers) labeled “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.003,” which stays very close to zero across all layers, starting around ~0.02 at layer 0 and approaching ~0.00 by the final layers; an orange dotted line (no markers) labeled “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.126,” which starts high near ~0.85 at layer 0, drops steeply over early layers (around ~0.40 by layer 1 and ~0.15 by about layer 5), then continues decreasing toward low values near ~0.03–0.06 through mid-to-late layers, with small late-layer bumps including a visible rise around layers ~19–22 (peaking near ~0.09 around ~21) before ending near ~0.05–0.06; and a green dash-dot line (no markers) labeled “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.080,” which also starts high near ~0.80 at layer 0, declines sharply to roughly ~0.28 by layer 1 and ~0.10 by about layer 5, then gradually decreases toward near-zero values (around ~0.02 by roughly layers 10–12) and remains close to ~0.00–0.01 through the final layers.
